standard: NFPA 13 (2019 edition) - Table 27.2.3.1.1, Equivalent Schedule 40 Steel Pipe Length Chart
note: Equivalent length in FEET of Schedule 40 steel pipe, keyed by the same nominalSize strings as reference/pipes/*.json. A size missing from a fitting's map is not published for that fitting (shown as a dash in the table) -- SprinklerHydraulicCalculator throws for that combination rather than assuming zero, and a caller can pass an explicit equivalentLengthFt instead. 10 in. and 12 in. are transcribed for completeness even though reference/pipes/*.json currently stops at 8 in.
cFactorBasisNote: Published lengths are in feet of C=120 pipe. SprinklerHydraulicCalculator rescales them for the segment's own C by (C/120)^1.85, which reproduces NFPA's published multipliers (0.713 at C=100, 1.16 at C=130, 1.33 at C=140, 1.51 at C=150). Note the direction: rougher pipe (lower C) needs FEWER equivalent feet, so dry/preaction steel at C=100 gets shorter lengths than printed here. The inverse form (120/C)^1.85 does not match the published factors. An explicitly supplied equivalentLengthFt on a fitting is never rescaled, since the caller's basis is unknown.
transcriptionNote: Transcribed from an image of the printed table, so tagged 'verify' until a second pass confirms it. Three oddities are transcribed as published, not corrected: the butterfly valve is 12 ft at 4 in. but 9 ft at 5 in.; the vane type flow switch is 30 ft at 4 in. but 16 ft at 6 in. (both non-monotonic, and both are the cells most worth re-reading against the printed page); and 1/2 in. appears only because NFPA 13 Sections 29.4/29.5 allow that size. Swing check values are averages, per the table's own footnote, because equivalent length varies with valve design.
